title: New Dark Vampire Fantasy Sets 2027 Release Date With Epic Trailer – Watch Now
content:
Vampires have been making a major comeback in popular media in recent years, with films, games, and anime reinventing the nocturnal blood-suckers to bring them back into the limelight. 2027 is ramping up to be a big year for the gothic creatures, with vampire-themed anime like Otaku Vampire’s Love Bite and The Record of a Fallen Vampire set to release throughout the year. Joining them is a brand-new series from Studio Teddy, the anime adaptation of Mercedes and the Waning Moon , an original series by Firehead that marries the concepts of isekai adventure with the romantic appeal of vampirism.

Mercedes and the Waning Moon is a unique spin on the isekai genre, taking a disgruntled, unnamed reincarnated individual and giving them a second chance at life as a vampire named Mercedes Grunewald, a descendant of vampire nobility forced to live in the countryside with her mother due to bad blood between her father. Unsure of her future or position in their house’s line of succession, Mercedes instead becomes a professional dungeon crawler. In anticipation for the anime’s January release and kicking off the new year, the anime adaptation revealed a stunning new trailer and promotional art you can find below.

Mercedes and the Waning Moon Promises Vampiric Romanticism With Isekai Adventure

The newly revealed trailer and key visual for Mercedes and the Waning Room depicts the titular Mercedes wielding her signature battle axe while surrounded by shattered glass teasing other characters that appear throughout the series. The main voice cast for the anime was also shared, which includes a star-studded cast consisting of Anna Nagase (Akane in Akane-banashi ) as Mercedes, Kenta Miyake (All Might in My Hero Academia ) as Benkei, Ryunosuke Watanuki (Okuhito in Blue Lock ) as Kuro, Junichi Suwabe (Eraser Head in My Hero Academia ) as Florian, Ai Kayano (Mikan in Danganronpa 2 ) as Ludia, Hina Omori as Margit, Miyu Tomita (Riko in Made in Abyss ) as Monica, and Sho Hayami (Sosuke in Bleach ) as Bernhard.

The anime adaptation of Firehead’s original series will be produced by Studio Teddy, an independent anime studio founded in 2014. A relatively newer studio, Teddy previously produced the main animation for I’ve Been Killing Slimes for 300 Years and Maxed Out My Level Season 2, with Mercedes and the Waning Moon being their first original animation project, but the studio has worked on a number of heavy-hitting anime series in a smaller capacity.

These other projects include key animation on Jujutsu Kaisen Season 2, key animation across multiple entries in the JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure franchise, and animation assistance on Sailor Moon Crystal . If that weren’t promising enough that Mercedes and the Waning Moon is going to be a hit, the director for the series is none other than Kunihisa Sugishima, best known for his work on Yu Gi Oh! Duel Monsters , as well as storyboarding credits on Code Geass and Higurashi .

Where To Find Mercedes and the Waning Moon

Mercedes and the Waning Moon will officially release as part of the Winter 2027 Anime season on Sundays beginning on January 10, 2027. As of writing, there is currently no official announcement when a global streaming service like Crunchyroll or HIDIVE will be picking up the anime to stream for global audiences. However, the original light novel series has been picked up and localized for English-speaking audiences by J-Novel Club. Available digitally under the title Mercedes and the Waning Moon: The Dungeoneering Feats of a Discarded Vampire Aristocrat , the first four volumes of the series are currently available directly through the publishers site for purchase as an e-book.

Originally a web novel written by Firehead that was uploaded to Shosetsuka ni Naro between 2018 to 2022, the Mercedes and the Waning Moon was eventually picked up for a print release by TO Books who collected the series into light novels and began publishing the books in 2021. The series is still ongoing, and has a manga adaptation that condenses the story into a graphic novel format. The manga is also available in English through J-Novel Club.

As of writing, even before the anime adaptaiton makes its official debut, Mercedes and the Waning Moon has an extremely impressive 200,000 copies in circulation. But how do you like the look of the new anime so far? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Ao no Hana Utsuwa no Mori Live-Action Series Gets 2-Episode Spinoff Drama on December 21
content:
NHK announced on Tuesday that a two-episode spinoff of the live-action series based on Yuki Kodama 's Ao no Hana Utsuwa no Mori (Blue Flower, Forest of Vessels) manga, titled Ao no Hana Utsuwa no Mori Spinoff Ano Ko no Kuchibeni (Blue Flower, Forest of Vessels Spinoff: That Girl's Lipstick), will air consecutively on NHK 's "Yorudora" programming block from December 21 at 11:00 p.m. JST. The spinoff episodes will run after the main series ends with its final episode on December 17.

The spinoff series will star:

• Kentarō Maeda as Fumiya Uno (second from left in image above)

• Riko as Sayaka Yoshizaki (third from left in image above)

• Misato Ugaki as Akane (leftmost)

• Menjo Kentarō as Ichise (rightmost)

The 15-minute spinoff drama centers on Fumiya, a young artisan working at Kōyō Kiln in Hasami, a town in Nagasaki prefecture famed for its pottery. The owner tasks Fumiya to create a new piece of pottery, and he confidently makes a prototype, but the lukewarm reaction of his colleagues including Aoko (from the main series), leaves him disheartened. To cheer him up, Sayaka, another colleague of Fumiya, invites him to a jazz live performance. When they arrive at the jazz bar, Fumiya finds his senior colleagues Ichinose and Akane performing.

The main series' Yōko Izumisawa is also writing the spinoff drama's script. Motohiro Hata performs the theme song "Fragments."

Yoshihiro Fukagawa is directing the series.

The manga takes place in Hasami, a town in Nagasaki prefecture famed for its pottery, and centers on Aoko, who is a ceramics painter, and her romance with a young man named Tatsuki who visits her studio.

Kodama ( Kids on the Slope ) launched the manga in Shogakukan 's Flowers magazine in March 2018, and ended it in March 2022. Shogakukan published the manga's 10th and final compiled book volume in August 2022.

title: Dragon Ball’s Official Canon is Missing Out on One of Dragon Ball GT’s Best Ideas
content:
One of the most tragic races in the Dragon Ball universe continues to get content made about them, but only in mostly non-canon timelines , which feels like a further twist of the knife. The Tuffles deserved much more dignified storytelling because their planet was taken from them by the Saiyans. Their peaceful race mostly focused on technological advances, and didn’t go out searching for conflict. It came to their front door when King Vegeta led the Saiyans in a war to takeover the planet.

The Tuffles are canon in terms of the Dragon Ball Z anime, but by manga standards they are not. Akira Toriyama reportedly created them for the anime franchise , so it’s a half-and-half canon argument. Explaining how the Saiyans took over Planet Vegeta, this also continued one of the enduring plot points of the Dragon Ball universe that Goku, Vegeta and the rest of the Z Fighters regularly have to clean up after their evil forefathers. The rooting interest isn’t simply the Saiyans are good and their enemies are evil. Sometimes context is needed for the full story.

Dragon Ball GT’s Canon Controversy Causes Confusion

The reason the Tuffles are a difficult topic is that their largest amount of screen time took place in non-canon releases Dragon Ball GT featured the Tuffles more than any other prior release thanks to the invention of Baby. The evil parasite wanted to eradicate the Saiyans and bring about the resurgence of the Tuffles. As the most iconic villain of the Dragon Ball GT series overall, it made the fanbase zero-in on the Tuffles’ lore and history.

Dragon Ball GT was eventually confirmed to not be a part of the official canon, so it sparked even more mystery around where the Tuffles could fall in the Dragon Ball story. The race is mentioned in Dragon Ball Super as it’s revealed that the Saiyans are still living in harmony with the Tuffles in Universe 6, but their main universe story needs to come back into the canon to further expand their journey. Fans can’t wipe their memory of the Baby arc, and that’s the most extensive story in their history. The only logical route forward is to feature them in the Dragon Ball Super manga’s future.

Super Must Bring Them Back

One of the fun parts of Dragon Ball ‘s multiverse is that it provides a fresh start for many arcs. The savagery the Saiyans showed in their war with the Tuffles can’t be undone, but the Z Fighters can visit Universe 6 and learn about the race. It may even provide a way in for them to take Baby’s now non-existent mission. Even though the Saiyans from Universe 6 are allies to Universe 7, the Tuffles might see them as bullies that eliminated their brethren. Or a group of the Tuffles might decide to wage war on the Z Fighters.

Imagine what it would then be like if Vegeta had to come to grips with his father’s atrocities while simultaneously defending the innocence of the current Saiyans through this new level of context? There are numerous forks in the road that could work for this story, but it’s got to get reintroduced with the Tuffles first. Do you think the Tuffles should return to the Dragon Ball story canon in the future? Let us know in the comments.

title: Live-Action Quiztopia Series Adds 13 Cast Members
content:
Netflix unveiled 13 new cast members for Quiztopia , its eight-episode live-action series of Reiichi Sugimoto and Shinkichi Kato 's Kokumin Quiz ( National Quiz ) manga, on Monday.

The new cast members all play characters who are enthusiastic fans of the National Quiz, and include:

• Kōji Ōkura as Anko, the proprietor of a suspicious snack bar, and who moves in the background of the story.

• THE STREET BEATS band's guitarist and vocalist OKI as a regular at Anko's snack bar

• Louis Kurihara as another regular at the snack bar

• Daikichi Sugawara, Kenichirō Tanabe, Umi Yamano, Ryō Katō, Himena Irei as homeless people

• Gaku Sano as Shigeki Mizumoto, a soccer player who lost his life at the National Quiz

• Sissonne comedy duo members Jirō and Shinobu Hasegawa as regulars at a restaurant who are crazy about the National Quiz

• Yoshihiro Nozoe and Yorie Yoshimoto as workers at the restaurant

Netflix describes the story:

The story takes place in an alternate Japan where Quiztopia, a national quiz show, has become the country's supreme governing authority. Under the National Quiz Law, any contestant who survives the quiz can have virtually any wish granted by the government — wealth, fame, the death of an enemy, the erasure of a criminal record, even ownership of a national landmark. The broadcast draws enormous audiences, and even the brutal forced labor awaiting eliminated contestants is treated as entertainment in this cheerfully dystopian society. At the center of it all is KK ( Takayuki Yamada ), the show's iconic host and the public's chief provocateur — who comes into contact with a group plotting to bring down Quiztopia, setting off an incident that could awaken people consumed by this seductive nightmare.

Takayuki Yamada (live-action Densha Otoko 's "Train Man," Bakuman. 's Akira Hattori, Gintama 's Elizabeth) stars in the series as KK.

The cast includes:

• Masahiro Takashima as as Commander Murakoshi, who leads the Reward and Punishment Squad responsible for carrying out penalties determined by the quiz results

• Eiko Koike as Shoko Kamijo, the producer behind Quiztopia

• Riko Ishida as Marii, a mysterious girl intent on killing KK

• Kana Kurashina as Ayako, Mari's mother and a central figure in the story;

• Kōji Seto as Seiji Nanbara, an activist plotting Quiztopia's downfall

• Renji Ishibashi as Takeshi Gokumazawa, the Prime Minister of Japan

• Rin Kataoka

• Yuzu Aoki

• Naruki Matsukawa

• Yūki Imai

• Shunsuke Daitō

• Akira Maehara

• Hoshi no Disco

• First Summer Uika

• Keiko Horiuchi

• Toshinori Omi

Teruyuki Yoshida (live-action An Older Guy's VR First Love , My Brother’s Husband ) is directing the series, and is also co-writing the scripts with Maggy. Yasunori Nishiki is composing the music.

The series premieres on Netflix on December 17.

Sugimoto and Kato serialized the manga in Kodansha 's Morning magazine from 1993 to 1995. Kodansha published four compiled book volumes for the manga. Ohta Publishing re-released the manga in two compiled book volumes in 2001.

title: Want More Godzilla? Check Out Netflix’s Anime Movie Trilogy
content:
After the release of Godzilla Minus Zero , the smash-hit follow-up to 2023’s Godzilla Minus One , fans of the kaiju franchise have been clamoring to find more content featuring their favorite reptilian titan. Thankfully, the Godzilla franchise has 72-years worth of content for fans to dive into, including Netflix’s three part film series from Toho Animation and Polygon Pictures. Consisting of Godzilla: Planet of the Monsters , Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle and Godzilla: The Planet Eater , this action-packed sci-fi trilogy tells a high-stakes story.

Initially introduced as a revenge journey that later pivots to focusing on the struggle between humans and nature, hubris, and the philosophy of what gives us an indomitable drive to survive, this unique Godzilla trilogy was penned by none other than Gen Urobuchi, a prolific and infamous writer known for his work on franchises like Puella Magi Madoka Magica , Psycho-Pass , and even legendary tokusatsu such as Kamen Rider Gaim . True to his other works, all three of these Godzilla films take their time unraveling their overarching narrative, using the legendary figure of Godzilla to aid in exploring the psychology of each of the main characters .

The Netflix Godzilla Trilogy Reinvents The Legendary Kaiju In a Fascinating Way

Opening with Godzilla: Planet of the Monsters in 2017 , the trilogy begins by introducing audiences to a group of human refugees returning to the planet Earth to attempt to recolonize it 20,000 years after being chased away by the titular kaiju. The film also introduces two alien species that worked in tandem when Earth was lost to the beast, known as the Exif, a group of religious zealots, as well as the technologically advanced Bilusaludo. After their failure to aid humanity in defeating Godzilla, humans emigrated to an exoplanet called “Tau-e.”

The film’s protagonist, Haruo Sakaki, holds a bitter hatred toward the kaiju and has made a vow to destroy it and reclaim Earth for humanity after deciding that Tau-e is inhabitable for human-kind’s continued existence. The first film follows many story beats akin to a typical revenge story, but as the plot unravels it becomes clear that the first film is aiming to set up a “humans versus nature” conflict. Without giving too many details away, Planet of the Monsters leaves off on a cliffhanger that leads perfectly into its 2018 follow-up film, Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle .

Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle introduces another fan-favorite kaiju : Mechagodzilla who aids the returning human cast in their efforts to defeat Godzilla. The film is a direct sequel, opening shortly after the first entry’s cliffhanger ending. The third and final film in the trilogy, The Planet Eater , leans heavily into themes of existential dread and human psychology, with the same extraterrestrial forces who once vowed to help humanity in their efforts now outwardly acting with hostility toward them due to differences in priorities when handling the threat of the giant kaiju threatening their recolonization efforts.

This film explores many classic story beats embedded into the roots of the Godzilla franchise as well, drawing comparisons between the beast and human-made tragedies. Directed in a collaborative effort by Kobun Shizuno ( Detective Conan, Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone ) and Hiroyuki Seshita ( Knights of Sidonia, Ajin ), the trilogy is uniquely positioned in how it presents these story beats, as it’s the first Godzilla trilogy to commit fully to some of the franchise’s sci-fi leanings and even giving Godzilla mutations akin to films like Shin Godzilla .

Godzilla ‘s Anime Trilogy’s Production Staff Knew Exactly What They Were Doing With The Iconic Monster

While the overall reception to the Netflix Godzilla trilogy is mixed in regards to how well the films stand as proper entries to the franchise, it’s clear to see what the filmmaking team wanted to do with the story. In that, all three films beautifully accomplish exactly what they set out to do. Gen Urobuchi’s scriptwriting prowess really hits its stride in the second film as the main cast’s goals begin to unravel as they reckon with the consequences of pitting advanced technology against a hulking beast that’s inhabited the Earth for well over 20,000 years.

Additionally, it’s easy to see just how well the directing duo Kobun Shizuno and Hiroyuki Seshita understand psychological storytelling as it pertains to science fiction as a genre. The pair are able to showcase stunning sci-fi action sequences and large-scale kaiju fights that are interspersed with deeply compelling conversations about humanities position on the intergalactic food chain.All of this is only amplified by the absolutely phenomenal vocal performances found throughout the film trilogy, including Mamoru Miyano’s role as the protagonist, Haruo Sakaki.

Mamoru Miyano has without a doubt positioned himself as an A-list casting choice for any anime series or film out there, with casting credits including legendary characters like Doma in Demon Slayer , Chrollo in Hunter x Hunter , and Light Yagami in Death Note . Other performances throughout the trilogy include other huge names in the industry, Takahiro Sakurai, Kana Hanazawa, Yuki Kaji, and Daisuke Ono.

For any Godzilla fan looking for a narratively compelling, bittersweet story of humanities conflict with nature, especially after the heartbreaking conclusion of Godzilla Minus Zero , there’s truly no better option than binging Netflix’s Godzilla trilogy. Have you checked out this trilogy yet? If so, what do you think of this take on Godzilla? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

Opening with Godzilla: Planet of the Monsters in 2017 , the trilogy begins by introducing audiences to a group of human refugees returning to the planet Earth to attempt to recolonize it 20,000 years after being chased away by the titular kaiju. The film also introduces two alien species that worked in tandem when Earth was lost to the beast, known as the Exif, a group of religious zealots, as well as the technologically advanced Bilusaludo. After their failure to aid humanity in defeating Godzilla, humans emigrated to an exoplanet called “Tau-e.”

The film’s protagonist, Haruo Sakaki, holds a bitter hatred toward the kaiju and has made a vow to destroy it and reclaim Earth for humanity after deciding that Tau-e is inhabitable for human-kind’s continued existence. The first film follows many story beats akin to a typical revenge story, but as the plot unravels it becomes clear that the first film is aiming to set up a “humans versus nature” conflict. Without giving too many details away, Planet of the Monsters leaves off on a cliffhanger that leads perfectly into its 2018 follow-up film, Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle .

Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle introduces another fan-favorite kaiju : Mechagodzilla who aids the returning human cast in their efforts to defeat Godzilla. The film is a direct sequel, opening shortly after the first entry’s cliffhanger ending. The third and final film in the trilogy, The Planet Eater , leans heavily into themes of existential dread and human psychology, with the same extraterrestrial forces who once vowed to help humanity in their efforts now outwardly acting with hostility toward them due to differences in priorities when handling the threat of the giant kaiju threatening their recolonization efforts.

This film explores many classic story beats embedded into the roots of the Godzilla franchise as well, drawing comparisons between the beast and human-made tragedies. Directed in a collaborative effort by Kobun Shizuno ( Detective Conan, Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone ) and Hiroyuki Seshita ( Knights of Sidonia, Ajin ), the trilogy is uniquely positioned in how it presents these story beats, as it’s the first Godzilla trilogy to commit fully to some of the franchise’s sci-fi leanings and even giving Godzilla mutations akin to films like Shin Godzilla .
Godzilla ‘s Anime Trilogy’s Production Staff Knew Exactly What They Were Doing With The Iconic Monster

While the overall reception to the Netflix Godzilla trilogy is mixed in regards to how well the films stand as proper entries to the franchise, it’s clear to see what the filmmaking team wanted to do with the story. In that, all three films beautifully accomplish exactly what they set out to do. Gen Urobuchi’s scriptwriting prowess really hits its stride in the second film as the main cast’s goals begin to unravel as they reckon with the consequences of pitting advanced technology against a hulking beast that’s inhabited the Earth for well over 20,000 years.

Additionally, it’s easy to see just how well the directing duo Kobun Shizuno and Hiroyuki Seshita understand psychological storytelling as it pertains to science fiction as a genre. The pair are able to showcase stunning sci-fi action sequences and large-scale kaiju fights that are interspersed with deeply compelling conversations about humanities position on the intergalactic food chain.All of this is only amplified by the absolutely phenomenal vocal performances found throughout the film trilogy, including Mamoru Miyano’s role as the protagonist, Haruo Sakaki.

Mamoru Miyano has without a doubt positioned himself as an A-list casting choice for any anime series or film out there, with casting credits including legendary characters like Doma in Demon Slayer , Chrollo in Hunter x Hunter , and Light Yagami in Death Note . Other performances throughout the trilogy include other huge names in the industry, Takahiro Sakurai, Kana Hanazawa, Yuki Kaji, and Daisuke Ono.

For any Godzilla fan looking for a narratively compelling, bittersweet story of humanities conflict with nature, especially after the heartbreaking conclusion of Godzilla Minus Zero , there’s truly no better option than binging Netflix’s Godzilla trilogy. Have you checked out this trilogy yet? If so, what do you think of this take on Godzilla? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

title: 'Giant Ojousama' Reveals Additional Cast, Character Promo
content:
The official X (formerly Twitter) account for the television anime adaptation of Q Nikumura 's Giant Ojousama manga revealed additional cast and three character promotional videos on Friday. The anime is scheduled to premiere in January 2027.

Cast Madoka Itou: Risa Imayanagi ( Nokemono-tachi no Yoru ) Stella: Rina Kawaguchi ( Needy Girl Overdose ) Gimlet: Ryoutarou Okiayu ( Kanan-sama wa Akumade Choroi )

Hiroshi Ikehata ( Witch Watch ) is directing at Tatsunoko Production . Yuu Satou ( Haite Kudasai, Takamine-san ) is handling the series composition and penning the script. Hajime Mitsuda ( Akiba's Trip The Animation ) is designing the characters.

Yuusuke Shirato (Dream Monster) ( Kunoichi Tsubaki no Mune no Uchi ), Kijibato (Dream Monster) ( Ijiranaide, Nagatoro-san 2nd Attack ending theme song composition), and Aira (Dream Monster) ( Kaya-chan wa Kowakunai opening theme song composition) are composing the music.

Nikumura originally posted the manga on Shounen Jump+ web magazine's Jump Rookie! section as an entry for the monthly award in December 2020. Following a readers vote, it won the Bronze Rookie Award for December. A total of four chapters were released by February 2021.

Sunday Webry began serializing the action comedy manga in July 2021. Shogakukan published the 13th volume on September 11, with the 14th volume scheduled to be released on December 11.

title: The Dragon Prince's Ill-Mated Betrothal Manga Ends, Gets 3-Chapter Epilogue
content:
Manga artist Sango Sansan 's manga adaptation of Nanaki Ichinose 's The Dragon Prince's Ill-Mated Betrothal light novel series ended with its 32nd chapter, which NTT Solmare 's Comic CMOA manga service published on September 17. With the manga's ending, Sansan also announced that author Ichinose has penned a manga-original epilogue story, which are being published in three chapters. Comic CMOA published epilogue chapter 33 on October 17 and chapter 34 on November 17.

Yen Press licensed the manga and will publish the first volume on January 26. The company describes the story:

Adeline, daughter of an earl, receives an offer of engagement from the Dragonkin Realm on her seventeenth birthday. All Dragonkins must find their "Mate," and they want her for their third prince. Soon, amid scorn and criticism, she realizes she's an unwilling participant in a twisted—and deadly—plot. But the story doesn't end there! 250 years later, history begins to repeat itself with another invitation...and the unknown secrets that lie beyond it.

Sansan launched the manga adaptation on Comic CMOA in July 2024. Kadokawa published the manga's fifth compiled book volume on November 17.

Ichinose launched the original story on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website in 2018. Kadokawa published the first novel volume with original character design by Noco Sugimachi in March 2024. The fourth volume shipped on November 25.

title: MangaPlaza Add Seven Seas Titles to Catalogue
content:
Some of the titles coming to the platform include:

• Mushoku Tensei - Jobless Reincarnation - Rifujin na Magonote, Yuka Fujikawa

• Though I Am an Inept Villainess: Tale of the Butterfly-Rat Body Swap in the Maiden Court - Satsuki Nakamura, Ei Ohitsuji

• The Exiled Heavy Knight Knows How to Game the System (Omnibus) - Nekoko, Brocco Lee, Jaian

• The Saint’s Magic Power is Omnipotent - Yuka Tachibana, Fujiazuki

• The Strange House - Uketsu, Kyō Ayano

The platform will also run a point reward promotion for all Seven Seas titles.

NTT Solmare Corp launched MangaPlaza , a digital contents library for manga and Japanese publications in the United States, in spring 2022. MangaPlaza offers original titles that have yet to get English releases, along with titles from other publishers such as Kodansha .

NTT Solmare is a subsidiary of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone West Corporation.

title: Sword Art Online Creator’s New Anime Has a Chance to Be the Next Big Hit
content:
Earlier this month, an action fantasy anime by the creator of Sword Art Online made its debut, and it’s already one of the most unique series in recent years. Sword Art Online is one of those 2010s classics that are still relevant to this day. Not only is the world-building incredible, but the exceptional storytelling, complex characters, and the exciting plot twists keep fans hooked to the show until the very end. The novel’s author, Reki Kawahara, doesn’t shy away from showing the brutality of the world where the story is set, just so fans are aware of the high stakes.

Throughout his career, Kawahara has worked on a few stories, and each of them stands out in one way or the other. This also includes Devil’s Crest that made its debut on Prime Video on November 6th. While the anime had a late start compared to the other Fall 2026 shows, it’s easily one of the best anime of the year. The anime is based on an ongoing novel written by Kawahara. While it’s too soon to determine if the anime is already a major hit, it has the potential to be one of the biggest hits in recent years. Luckily, the premiere generated enough hype, especially considering fans of Sword Art Online would be interested in another show by the same creator.

Devil’s Crest Deserves to Be a Bigger Hit Than Sword Art Online

The story is still in its initial phase as it introduces fans to the main characters, the unique premise, and the expansive world-building. What truly sets this anime apart is that it offers a completely new outlook on stories centering around a virtual reality game. In Sword Art Online , the characters in the first major arc were physically trapped inside a virtual reality MMORPG and could not log out. This premise isn’t only limited to Sword Art Online , but many such anime focus on the characters entering the game world as they try to survive while also trying to figure out a way to return home.

However, Devils’ Crest switches things up by bringing the virtual reality into the real world. The story focuses on a group of middle school students who never could’ve imagined that playing a new virtual reality game would not only turn their world upside down, but also plunge their world into chaos. Instead of being trapped inside the video game world, they realize that the game world blends into the real world, raising the stakes much higher than any other isekai show.

Another thing that sets Devils’ Crest apart is that it has a much darker tone, as the first couple of episodes portray an unimaginable level of brutality and gruesome moments. This is something even Sword Art Online didn’t feature , even though it has intense moments throughout the story. The anime has released four episodes as of now, and it’s safe to say that the story is finally taking shape as the central group is now learning how to defeat the monsters and save their world.

How are you liking Devils’ Crest so far, and would you be keeping up with the weekly episodes? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Killer Shark in Another World Anime Adaptation Announced
content:
An anime adaptation of Killer Shark in Another World manga by Kuboken has been announced. A teaser visual and trailer were also released. Studio Lings is animating the series.

Shige Fukase is directing the anime adaptation with Shigeru Murakoshi in charge of the series composition. Nozomi Ikuyama is on character designs, while Iroha Mitsuki is on shark design, and Keiji Inai is composing the music.

Kill Time Communication’s Comic Valkyrie magazine is serializing the manga since 2020. Seven Seas Entertainment is publishing the title in English, describing it as: Everyone thought Shiromi Lovecut-Toothrough was the worst summoner in the world. But after she summons Sharkiller, a creature capable of transforming into Hollywood’s most ferocious B-movie sharks, nobody’s laughing now! In fact, they’re running for their lives! With her bloodthirsty buddy chomping at the bit to kill everyone in sight, can Shiromi defeat the Demon King and end his reign of terror? Or maybe the realm would be better off if she didn’t…?
